title: Infinitely many solutions (the same line)
subtitle: Systems of two linear equations in two variables · 12 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **12 of the official questions in Systems of two linear equations in two variables are this one** — 2 Easy, 3 Medium, 7 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The question says the system has infinitely many solutions or at least one solution, or asks which point lies on both graphs 'for each real number'.
- You may need to find a constant, choose the second equation, or evaluate statements marked I and II.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Put both equations in the same form, either standard Ax + By = C or y = mx + b.
- 2) Infinitely many solutions means one equation is a constant multiple of the other: x-coefficients, y-coefficients AND constants all in the same ratio.
- Set up that ratio and solve for the unknown constant.
- 3) For 'at least one solution', an intersecting line (a different slope) also counts, not only the same line.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Useful for a constant: add a slider for the constant and adjust it until the two lines overlap exactly.
For choosing a second equation, graph each choice and see which one sits on top of the given line.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You match the slopes but forget the constants must also be in the same ratio, which gives parallel lines, not the same line.
On 'at least one solution' questions, you wrongly rule out an intersecting line because you think only identical lines qualify.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You match the slopes but forget the constants must also be in the same ratio, which gives parallel lines, not the same line.
On 'at least one solution' questions, you wrongly rule out an intersecting line because you think only identical lines qualify.
